chapters.title: Before
chapters.teaser: The eldest of twelve children, growing up beside the railway at Stoford and working on the land.

chapters.title: Why he went
chapters.teaser: Henry went to France in 1915, before anyone was made to go. What made a young farm hand volunteer?

chapters.title: Becoming a soldier
chapters.teaser: From the base depot to the trenches: the months that turned a farm hand into a rifleman. Step inside a trench, try the gas drill, censor a letter and learn to talk like a Tommy.

record.source: His service and casualty records, as summarised by the Rifles Berkshire and Wiltshire Museum

entries.entry: Went to France with the Somerset Light Infantry. His casualty record gives 22 June 1915; the medal roll gives 22 July.
Posted to the 8th Entrenching Battalion, digging and road-mending behind the lines.
Joined the 1st Battalion, Somerset Light Infantry.

chapters.title: The Line
chapters.teaser: The first day of the Battle of the Somme. Henry's battalion crosses No Man's Land towards a German strongpoint called the Quadrilateral.
chapters.contentNote: This chapter describes a battle in which many men were killed and wounded, including Henry.

record.source: His service and casualty records, as summarised by the Rifles Berkshire and Wiltshire Museum

entries.entry: Admitted to 47 Casualty Clearing Station with a gunshot wound to the face.
Record also lists a gunshot wound to the left hand: 12th Field Ambulance, then a Canadian hospital.
Posted to the 1st Battalion, Wiltshire Regiment.

chapters.title: Meanwhile in Blighty
chapters.teaser: While Henry was away, life at home carried on. What did his family know, and what did they hear?

chapters.title: The end of the war
chapters.teaser: Nearly two more years of war with a new regiment: the Somme again, Belgium, Ypres, a friend from home, one stripe, and a March morning in 1918 that changed everything.
chapters.contentNote: This chapter describes fighting, men being killed, the death of a young soldier Henry knew (an imagined story), and Henry being taken prisoner.

record.source: His service and casualty records, as summarised by the Rifles Berkshire and Wiltshire Museum

entries.entry: Fined a day's pay for being absent from a 2.30pm parade until 9.45pm.
In hospital in France with an inflamed middle ear.
Reported missing, C Company, east of Frémicourt.

chapters.title: After
chapters.teaser: Home, Nell, the charabanc and the lorries, the bird hospital in the shed, Weymouth for his chest, and the memories he carried to the end of his life.
chapters.contentNote: This chapter touches on how the war stayed with Henry in later life.

record.source: His service and casualty records, as summarised by the Rifles Berkshire and Wiltshire Museum

entries.entry: Discharged to the Class Z Reserve.

chapters.title: Legacy
chapters.teaser: In August 2026 four of his descendants walked the ground where he fought. This chapter ends with room for your own memories of him.
